arxiv-1807-03375.title: Debashis Ghosh
arxiv-1807-03375.description: Abstract Predictive directions for individualized treatment selection in clinical trials Summary In many clinical trials, individuals in different subgroups have experience differential treatment effects. This leads to individualized differences in treatment benefit. In this article, we introduce the general concept of predictive directions, which are risk scores motivated by potential outcomes considerations.

arxiv-2304-04292.title: Proof Generation for CDCL Solvers Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination
arxiv-2304-04292.creator: Mate Soos, Randal E. Bryant
arxiv-2304-04292.description: Abstract Traditional Boolean satisfiability (SAT) solvers based on the conflict-driven clause-learning (CDCL) framework fare poorly on formulas involving large numbers of parity constraints. The CryptoMiniSat solver augments CDCL with Gauss-Jordan elimination to greatly improve performance on these formulas. Integrating the tbuddy proof-generating BDD library into CryptoMiniSat enables it to generate unsatisfiability proofs when using Gauss-Jordan elimination.

arxiv-2404-12865.title: A minimal model of boosting and waning in a recurrent seasonal epidemic
arxiv-2404-12865.description: Abstract We propose a model of the immunity to a cyclical epidemic disease taking account not only of seasonal boosts during the infectious season, but also of residual immunity remaining from one season to the next. The focus is on the exponential waning process over successive cycles, imposed on the temporal distribution of infections or exposures over a season.

arxiv-2410-05109.title: Secure Software/Hardware Hybrid In-Field Testing for System-on-Chip Thanks: 1 These authors contributed equally to this work. This work has been supported by DAIS (https://dais-project.eu/), which has received funding from the ECSEL Joint Undertaking (JU) under grant agreement No 101007273. The JU r
arxiv-2410-05109.creator: Saleh Mulhem 1 , Christian Ewert 1 , Andrija Nešković, Amrit Sharma Poudel, Christoph Hübner, Mladen Berekovic, and Rainer Buchty
arxiv-2410-05109.description: Abstract Modern Systems-on-Chip (SoCs) incorporate built-in self-test (BIST) modules deeply integrated into the device’s intellectual property (IP) blocks. Such modules handle hardware faults and defects during device operation. As such, BIST results potentially reveal the internal structure and state of the device under test (DUT) and hence open attack vectors.

We discuss how desirable it is that Large Language Models (LLMs 1 1 1 We mean by ‘LLM’ fully trained models like ChatGPT4 that can be accessed by users via a web interface.

arxiv-2507-06707.title: Multiscale Approximation as a Bias-Reducing Strategy for Scalar and Manifold-Valued Functions
arxiv-2507-06707.creator: Asaf Abas, Nir Sharon
arxiv-2507-06707.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Asaf Abas, Nir Sharon. We study the bias–variance tradeoff within a multiscale approximation framework. Our approach utilizes a given quasi-approximation operator, repeatedly applied in an error-correction scheme over a hierarchical data structure. We introduce a new bias measurement, the bias ratio, to quantitatively assess the improvements made by multiscale approximations and demonstrate that this multiscale strategy effectively reduces the bias component of the approximation error, thereby providing a more flexible and robust framework for addressing scattered data approximation problems.

arxiv-2508-07750.title: Learning to Align, Aligning to Learn: A Unified Approach for Self-Optimized Alignment
arxiv-2508-07750.creator: Haowen Wang, Yun Yue, Zhiling Ye, Shuowen Zhang, Lei Fan, Jiaxin Liang, Jiadi Jiang, Cheng Wei, Jingyuan Deng, Xudong Han, Ji Li, Chunxiao Guo, Peng Wei, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu
arxiv-2508-07750.description: Abstract Alignment methodologies have emerged as a critical pathway for enhancing language model alignment capabilities. While SFT (supervised fine-tuning) accelerates convergence through direct token-level loss intervention, its efficacy is constrained by offline policy trajectory. In contrast, RL(reinforcement learning) facilitates exploratory policy optimization, but suffers from low sample efficiency and stringent dependency on high-quality base models.

arxiv-2511-01484.title: Enhancing Non-Terrestrial Network Performance with Free Space Optical Links and Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces
arxiv-2511-01484.creator: Shunyuan Shang, Emna Zedini, and Mohamed-Slim Alouini
arxiv-2511-01484.description: Abstract The integration of non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), which include high altitude platform (HAP) stations and intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) into communication infrastructures has become a crucial area of research to address the increasing requirements for connectivity and performance in the post-5G era.

arxiv-2511-06232.title: Scaling Laws and In-Context Learning: A Unified Theoretical Framework
arxiv-2511-06232.creator: Sushant Mehta, Ishan Gupta
arxiv-2511-06232.description: Abstract In-context learning (ICL) enables large language models to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations without parameter updates. Despite extensive empirical studies, a principled understanding of ICL emergence at scale remains more elusive. We present a unified theoretical framework connecting scaling laws to ICL emergence in transformers.

arxiv-2512-17189.title: Anatomical Region-Guided Contrastive Decoding: A Plug-and-Play Strategy for Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical VLMs
arxiv-2512-17189.creator: Xiao Liang, Chenxi Liu, Zhi Ma, Di Wang, Bin Jing, Quan Wang, Yuanyuan Shi
arxiv-2512-17189.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xiao Liang, Chenxi Liu, Zhi Ma, Di Wang, Bin Jing, Quan Wang, Yuanyuan Shi. Medical Vision-Language Models (MedVLMs) show immense promise in clinical applicability. However, their reliability is hindered by hallucinations, where models often fail to derive answers from visual evidence, instead relying on learned textual priors.

arxiv-2601-07921.title: Charting the Flavour Structure of Dark Matter
arxiv-2601-07921.creator: Simone Biondini, Admir Greljo, Xavier Ponce Díaz, Alessandro Valenti
arxiv-2601-07921.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Simone Biondini, Admir Greljo, Xavier Ponce Díaz, Alessandro Valenti. What flavour structure of t t -channel thermal dark matter remains compatible with current flavour physics and direct detection bounds? We broadly chart the space of hypotheses using the framework of flavour symmetries and their breaking patterns. We then focus on scenarios in which the fermionic dark matter and its scalar mediator are flavour singlets, falling into the class of rank-1 flavour violation .

pmc-10571942.title: DNA Hypomethylation in the TNF-Alpha Gene Predicts Rheumatoid Arthritis Classification in Patients with Early Inflammatory Symptoms
pmc-10571942.creator: Rujiraporn Pitaksalee, Rekha Parmar, Richard Hodgett, Paul Emery, Frederique Ponchel
pmc-10571942.description: Biomarkers for the classification of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and particularly for anti-citrullinated peptide antibody (ACPA)-negative patients, remain an important hurdle for the early initiation of treatment. Taking advantage of DNA-methylation patterns specific to early RA, quantitative methylation-specific qPCR (qMSP) offers a robust technology for the development of biomarkers. We developed assays and established their value as RA classification biomarkers.

pmc-11436453.title: Disuse atrophy of articular cartilage can be restored by mechanical reloading in mice
pmc-11436453.creator: Masato Nomura, Hideki Moriyama, Yoshio Wakimoto, Yasushi Miura
pmc-11436453.description: BackgroundModerate mechanical stress generated by normal joint loading and movements helps maintain the health of articular cartilage. Despite growing interest in the pathogenesis of cartilage degeneration caused by reduced mechanical stress, its reversibility by mechanical reloading is less understood. This study aimed to investigate the response of articular cartilage exposed to mechanical reloading after unloading in vivo and in vitro.

pmc-11514692.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Optimal Antibiotic Prescribing on Discharge from the Hospital to Nursing Homes
pmc-11514692.creator: Jon Furuno, Michelle Zhou, Christopher Crnich, Dominic Chan, Caitlin McCracken, Sally Jolles, Brie Noble, Jessina McGregor, YoungYoon Ham, Emily Shephard, Seiko Izumi
pmc-11514692.description: Background: Up to half of antibiotics used in nursing homes (NHs) are initiated in acute care hospitals prior to nursing home admission. Optimizing antibiotic prescribing on hospital discharge presents an opportunity to improve NH antibiotic use. We aimed to identify barriers and facilitators to optimal antibiotic prescribing on discharge from the hospital to NHs.

pmc-11678822.title: Unveiling the Potential of Cmax f2 Factor Applied to Pilot Bioavailability/Bioequivalence Studies—A Case Study with Pazopanib Drug Products
pmc-11678822.creator: Sara Carolina Henriques, Ana Leblanc, Sérgio Simões, Marlene Fonseca, Francisco Luís Pimentel, Luis Almeida, Nuno Elvas Silva, Im-Sook Song
pmc-11678822.description: Background: When companies are uncertain about the potential of a new formulation to be bioequivalent to a Reference product, it is common practice to carry out downsized pilot studies as a gatekeeping in vivo strategy to decide whether to move forward or not with a full-size pivotal study.

pmc-11689163.title: IMPLEMENTATION OF A VIRTUAL FALL PREVENTION PROGRAM IN OLDER VETERANS
pmc-11689163.creator: Katherine Ritchey
pmc-11689163.description: Though virtual platforms have increased in popularity few studies have explored the implementation and benefit of a virtually-based fall prevention program. MOVing FREEly (Multicomponent Otago Virtual Falls Reduction Exercise and Education program) is a VA-based fall prevention program delivered entirely over a virtual care platform.

pmc-12952640.title: Klotho levels and biological age acceleration: Insights from a diverse cohort of middle-aged and elderly individuals
pmc-12952640.creator: Mengna Huang, Guoxin Huang, Chaoshen Wu, Lei Zhu, Bin Pei, Hongwei Wang, Da Qian, Puzhao Wu
pmc-12952640.description: ObjectiveAging is characterized by progressive physiological and psychological changes, leading to decreased cellular metabolism and increased vulnerability to age-related diseases.Methods.In this study, we examined the relationship between circulating Klotho levels and biological age acceleration (BAA) in a representative cohort of middle-aged and older adults.

pmc-13043730.title: Distinction between primary and metastatic mucinous ovarian carcinoma from histopathology images using deep learning
pmc-13043730.creator: Ming-Yi Zhang, Bin Liu, Zhao-Juan Qin, Yue-Di Zhang, Zhi-Qian Li, Rui-Zhi Liu, Zhi-Xiang Xia, Qiong-Xian Long, Jia Xu, Xiao-Li Mou, Lian-Sha Tang, Hong-Shuai Li, Wen-Jun Meng, Ai Zheng, Yang-Mei Shen, Ji-Yan Liu
pmc-13043730.description: Accurately distinguishing between primary and gastrointestinal metastatic mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) is crucial but remains highly challenging. We developed and validated the MOC Origin Prediction Model (MOCOPM), the deep learning model specifically designed to predict the origin of MOC from histopathology images.

pmc-13052549.title: Genotype-phenotype correlations in patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic titin variants from the Swiss Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy Registry
pmc-13052549.creator: Nina Alissa Schätti, Siv Fokstuen, Argelia Medeiros-Domingo, Umberto Maccio, Matthias P Nägele, Fran Mikulicic, Andreas J Flammer, Lorraine Sazgary, Robert Manka, Verena Charlotte Wilzeck, Felix Tanner, Christian Grebmer, Annina Salome Vischer, Katja E Odening, Marina Rieder, Frank Ruschitzka, Corin
pmc-13052549.description: BackgroundTruncating variants in the titin gene (TTNtv) are associated with cardiomyopathy, mainly dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). The clinical presentation and outcomes of arrhythmogenic phenotypes in these patients are scarcely studied.Methods and resultsThis was a retrospective Swiss national study including 46 cardiomyopathy patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) TTNtv. 63% were male and median age at diagnosis was 47 years.

pmc-13145915.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A634 POLYVASCULAR BURDEN DEFINES A VASCULAR PHENOTYPE ASSOCIATED WITH WORSE FUNCTIONAL OUTCOME AFTER ISCHEMIC STROKE
pmc-13145915.creator: Jelena Stanarcevic, Stanarcevic Predrag, Dejana Jovanovic, Slobodan Cvetkovic
pmc-13145915.description: Background and aimsPost-stroke prognosis is mainly guided by neurological severity, while cumulative systemic vascular disease burden is rarely considered. Atherosclerotic involvement across multiple vascular territories may define a polyvascular phenotype influencing recovery beyond stroke severity. We assessed whether polyvascular burden is associated with functional and patient-reported outcomes after ischemic stroke and explored its relevance for phenotype-guided secondary prevention.

pmc-13205943.title: Determinants of Health-Related Quality of Life After Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Systematic Review
pmc-13205943.creator: Panagiota Peleka, Olympia Konstantakopoulou, Aglaia Katsiroumpa, Maria Katharaki, Olga Siskou, Daphne Kaitelidou, Petros Galanis
pmc-13205943.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Health-related quality of life after acute coronary syndromes is determined by multiple factors, with sex, age and depression being among the most frequent.Comorbidity, lack of social support and living alone are associated with significant quality-of-life decline, while a higher baseline quality of life can be a major protective factor for long-term recovery.

pmc-13404090.title: Cost-effectiveness of using Intravenous Ferric Carboxymaltose compared to Intravenous Iron Sucrose for treatment of iron deficiency anemia in pregnancy
pmc-13404090.creator: Beena Joshi, Tejal Varekar, Revathy R, Kiran Sangwan, Deepti Tandon, Ragini Kulkarni, Shahina Begum
pmc-13404090.description: BackgroundIron deficiency anemia (IDA) in pregnancy is a major public health concern in India, contributing significantly to adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes. Intravenous iron sucrose (IV ISC) is widely used; however, its low permissible dose necessitates multiple visits, reducing adherence and increasing out-of-pocket expenditure.

pmc-13408861.title: Optimizing adult nutrition and mating duration to improve mass rearing of Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi
pmc-13408861.creator: KT Shivakumara, SS Udikeri, T. Venkatesan, T. Sudha, MC Keerthi, M. Mohan, C. Manjunatha, K. Ashok, GS Guruprasad, SG. Rayar
pmc-13408861.description: Chrysoperla zastrowi sillemi (CZS) is an important predatory lacewing used in biological pest control across protected and open-field systems due to its high predation efficiency and insecticide tolerance. However, current mass-rearing practices are insufficient to meet commercial needs, primarily because of poor-quality production and low fecundity.

pmc-13531211.title: First-in-Human Mechanical Leaflet Modification of Native Aortic Stenosis During TAVR
pmc-13531211.creator: Danny Dvir, Amjad Abu Salman, Philippe Taieb, Shemy Carasso, Rami Jubeh, Arik Wolak, Elias Hellou, Michael Glikson, Anna Turyan

pmc-13556869.title: 517. The changes of plasma Nectin-4 levels during 12 weeks of naltrexone treatment in patients with alcohol use disorder
pmc-13556869.creator: M-C Chang, S-C Meng, M-C Huang
pmc-13556869.description: BackgroundNectin-4 is a cell adhesion molecule essential for maintaining cell-cell integrity. Previous studies have demonstrated elevated plasma levels of the extracellular domain of Nectin-4 in patients with heroin and ketamine dependence, which correlated with the severity of dependence. However, the role of Nectin-4 in alcohol use disorder (AUD) and its alterations during abstinence following naltrexone treatment remain unclear.

pmc-13568994.title: Essential, Yet Precarious, Mistreated, Sick and Medicalized: A Sequential Explanatory Mixed‐Methods Study on Homecare Aides in Spain
pmc-13568994.creator: Albert Navarro‐Giné, Pedro Ferrer‐Rosende, Maria Feijoo‐Cid, Sergio Salas‐Nicás, Laura Esteve‐Matalí, Valeria Stuardo‐Ávila, María Isabel Fernández‐Cano
pmc-13568994.description: BackgroundHomecare aides (HCAs) are professional non‐family caregivers, who support dependent individuals to live at home with dignity; yet in Spain they remain understudied and vulnerable, often facing precarious working conditions. We aimed to characterize HCAs’ employment, living conditions, health, and exposure to workplace violence and harassment, considering migrant background as a key axis of inequality.
